subject.title: Google Chat: Add user OAuth support for reactions and media uploads

question: Which delegated Google Chat identity model should the bundled plugin support for user-auth-only operations, and how should that identity be selected and stored?
rationale: Per-user OAuth and domain-wide delegation differ in consent, administrator control, sender attribution, token lifecycle, and blast radius; implementing either without an explicit contract could expose long-lived credentials or send messages as an unexpected user.

options.title: Scoped user OAuth flow
options.body: Add a plugin-owned login flow that obtains only the required Chat scopes, stores refresh credentials through approved secret/token surfaces, and explicitly binds each account to the consenting sender identity.

options.title: Domain-wide delegation only
options.body: Require Workspace administrators to configure service-account impersonation and a delegated subject, trading consumer usability for centralized organizational control.

options.title: Retain app authentication
options.body: Keep service-account-only behavior and pursue graceful reaction/media fallbacks without enabling user-attributed Google Chat actions.

recommendation.title: Scoped user OAuth flow
recommendation.body: Add a plugin-owned login flow that obtains only the required Chat scopes, stores refresh credentials through approved secret/token surfaces, and explicitly binds each account to the consenting sender identity.
